basis: Defining extrasystoles, microcephaly and persistent hyperpigmentation; short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Recurrent cutaneous purpura associated with immune-complex small-vessel inflammation and polyclonal hyperglobulinemia; no intrinsic blood-cell or coagulation disorder.
Neoplasm occupying the spinal epidural compartment; vertebral bone invasion is not required by this concept.
Luteinized ovarian stromal cells cause gonadal endocrine dysfunction and androgen excess; associated hypertension does not establish direct vascular injury.
Ocular and lacrimal defects define syndrome; maxillary hypoplasia and clinodactyly occur in 80-99%, tricuspid regurgitation in 30-79%; ear shape alone adds no axis.
Congenital ineffective erythropoiesis and anemia; hepatomegaly and hemolytic jaundice alone do not establish hepatic injury.
Formate toxicity defines metabolic acidosis, CNS injury and toxic visual-system dysfunction; transient hypertension and terminal respiratory failure add no axis.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; neurodevelopmental impairment 2/2 with documented brain injury, muscle weakness 2/2 and external ophthalmoplegia 1/1.
Developmental disability and seizures define CNS disease; cardiac defects individually affect at most 2/9, and their overlap prevents establishing a combined frequency.
Congenital unilateral malformation and enlargement of renal calyces.
Invasive chlamydial lymphatic infection; lymphadenopathy is not a blood-cell disorder. Proctocolitis is presentation-dependent; the Mycobacterium definition is inconsistent.
Carcinoma originating in the endometrium, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no metastatic site is specified.
Cerebral inflammation defines the affected organ; the generic definition does not establish an infectious or autoimmune etiology.
Congenital duplication of part of the alimentary tract.
Strabismus occurs in 3/7; cerebral visual impairment remains neurologic. Osteopenia in 3/7 is not clearly direct rather than secondary to immobility or treatment.
Familial thoracic aortic structural disease; connective-tissue abnormalities concern the vascular wall. Iris morphology alone does not establish ocular dysfunction.
CNS neoplasia is a defining organ association; prostate has no axis. This susceptibility concept does not itself demonstrate existing brain injury.
Congenital absence or severe underdevelopment of lung tissue; associated malformations are unspecified.
Acquired transmissible prion infection causes progressive neuronal loss, particularly in the cerebellum; weakness and incontinence are neurologic manifestations.
True intrauterine HSV classically damages skin (~95%), CNS (~65%) and eyes (~40%); individual CNS malformations can each be under 30%. Neonatal presentations vary.
Neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in 6/7; ptosis 2/7 and other individual eye or renal defects 1/7 do not clearly establish common additional organ damage.
Cavernous vascular lesion arising in brain or meninges; both vascular nature and CNS location define it. This is not a blood-cell neoplasm.
Acro-renal syndrome is defined by congenital limb and kidney malformations; recessive inheritance does not change these organ assignments.
Renal epithelial carcinoma associated with Xp11/TFE3 rearrangement; no other primary or metastatic organ involvement is established.
Microcephaly and skeletal dysplasia define syndrome; microphthalmia and microdontia/microglossia each occur in 1/1 assessed, with limited denominators; renal ectopia <30%.
